links.outcome: Radiologist performance with vs without AI-CAD vs standalone AI
links.effect: No significant difference with vs without AI (AUC 0.844 vs 0.710, p=0.146; sensitivity 76.5% vs 50.0%, p=0.135). Standalone AI beat unassisted radiologists on specificity (94.6% vs 91.9%) and recall (5.9% vs 8.6%).
links.quote: Diagnostic performances of the radiologists did not significantly differ with and without AI-CAD assistance.

links.outcome: Cancers missed by standalone AI-CAD and detected by supplementary ultrasound
links.effect: AI-CAD missed 10/29 cancers (34%). Of these, 9 were also rated BI-RADS 1–2 by radiologists and were detected by same-day supplementary ultrasound.
links.quote: All of these 9 patients had dense breasts, and subsequent ultrasound examinations revealed suspicious lesions, which were then diagnosed through ultrasound-guided biopsies.

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance of radiologists using AI assistance versus stand-alone AI
links.effect: Radiologists with AI-CAD versus stand-alone AI-CAD: sensitivity 76.5% in both; specificity 92.3% vs 93.8%; AUC 0.844 vs 0.851; recall rates 8.8% vs. 7.4%; no statistically significant differences.
links.quote: Radiologists with AI-CAD assistance showed the same sensitivity (76.5%) and similar specificity (92.3% vs 93.8%), AUC (0.844 vs 0.851), and recall rates (8.8% vs. 7.4%) compared to standalone AI-CAD.

links.outcome: Local AI missed-cancer rate compared with previously published same-platform performance
links.effect: The local AI-CAD missed-cancer rate was 34% (10/29), compared with 11–19.4% in previously published studies using the same platform.
links.quote: However, the false-negative rate of AI-CAD, also known as the missed cancer rate, was 34% (10/29), which was higher than previously published studies using the same platform at 11–19.4% [12] , [28] .

links.outcome: Supplementary ultrasound detection of cancers missed by AI and mammography interpretation
links.effect: Supplementary ultrasound identified suspicious lesions in 9 cancers missed by both AI-CAD and radiologists on mammography. All 9 patients had dense breasts; ultrasound-guided biopsies established the diagnoses.
links.quote: All of these 9 patients had dense breasts, and subsequent ultrasound examinations revealed suspicious lesions, which were then diagnosed through ultrasound-guided biopsies.
